features.title: Release each package and service at its own version
features.description: bh's release script makes one version for the whole repository. It moves into `@bh/config` as `bh-release`, which versions each package and service on its own, so bh and every app follow the same rules and a package nothing touched keeps its version.
today: `scripts/release.mjs`, run by `.github/workflows/release.yml` on every push to main, tags one version for every package from the conventional commits since the last tag that touch `packages/` or `copy.json`: `v0.1.0` to `v0.6.1`, each with a GitHub release listing its commits;
bh's packages say `0.0.1` in their `package.json`; the gateway writes the release's version into each package of a copy (`apps/api/src/library/copy.ts:147` in gateway);
the docs' Versions and updates page (`apps/docs/content/getting-started/versions.doc.yaml`) says bh has one version for all its packages;
no app has a version tag; gateway, signals and wallet-passes say a fixed `0.1.0` in their `package.json`;
the apps already write conventional commits (`feat(web): …`, `fix(db): …`).
chosen: Every package and every service has its own version, since not every one changes on every push (your answer). A version is a tag `<package name>@<version>` (`@bh/ui@0.7.0`, `@tickets/web@0.3.2`) with a GitHub release of its notes; no release commits.

Everything stays below 1.0.0 until you say a package is ready, and that package goes to 1.0.0 by hand (your answer). Below it, bh's rule: a breaking change (`!`, `BREAKING CHANGE:`) makes a minor version, and `feat`, `fix` and `perf` a patch; `build` and `chore(deps)` make a patch too (your answer); any other type makes none and goes out with the next. From 1.0.0, a breaking change makes a major version and a feature a minor one.
A commit belongs to each package whose folder it touches, whatever its scope says. Root files (the lockfile, the root `package.json`) belong to none.

A service (an app under `apps/`) also takes a patch when a workspace package it depends on makes a version, the vendored bh copy included, so its version changes whenever its build does. bh's own packages don't pass versions on: a package's version says its own code changed.
An app's release skips `packages/bh/*`, which carry bh's versions.
A bh package with no tag of its own takes `v0.6.1` as its last version; an app's package with none starts at 0.1.0.

plan.title: Move the release logic into `@bh/config` as `bh-release`, versioning each package
plan.description: `scripts/release.mjs` and its tests move to `@bh/config` (`bin/release.mjs`, beside `bh-lint`, `bh-format` and `bh-madge`), so the gateway's copy brings it to every app; `bh-release` joins `copy.json`'s `rename`, for items-core's `bw`. It finds the workspace's packages from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, gives each the commits since its last tag that touch its folder, bumps each by the rules above, and passes a service's dependencies' versions on to it, read from the `package.json`s. Without `--publish` it says what each would become; with it, it tags each and makes its GitHub release. A repository says which folders it skips and which are services (a `bhRelease` field in the root `package.json`, or the like).
